card.band: 8h. Frontier agents implement the basic limiter but miss the config surface, signal-specific behaviour, the metrics and the fake-clock semantics. Buckets by signal, algorithm and config. A weaker model stops at a single-key traces limiter.
card.cheat: A no-op passthrough passes none of the drop-count cases. Hidden tests use only public APIs, so special-casing is impossible.
card.grading: Hidden Go tests use public factory/config/consumer APIs with a fake clock and check admitted and dropped counts, error codes, per-key isolation, concurrency and config errors. Several hundred table cases. The existing suites of neighbouring processors are the regression gate.
card.reference: Our own implementation, expected 1500+ lines including tests and docs, modelled on the upstream issue discussion. It is not merged upstream in this form.
card.task: /app ships a pruned snapshot at the pinned commit. The agent adds a ratelimitprocessor component covering traces, logs and metrics. It needs per-key (attribute-derived) token-bucket and sliding-window limits, burst, a throttle-or-drop mode that returns the right errors, a dynamic-rate hook, telemetry metrics, config validation and a factory registered in the builder.

facts.claim: Issue #35204 'Rate Limit Processor' exists in opentelemetry-collector-contrib, opened 2024-09-16, still open, labelled Accepted Component
Issue #35204 has no linked branches or pull requests, so no upstream implementation exists to copy

The issue is a design discussion: proposed ratelimit processor with per-signal sections, a grouping block (strict/relaxed), tbf settings, and no fixed config schema; maintainer suggested error, discard or backpressure and rate-limit metrics
Release v0.163.0 exists (released 14 Oct, per GitHub release page)
The v0.163.0 changelog contains no rate limit processor or ratelimit component (only a yang_grpc receiver security.rate_limiting fix)
No ratelimit processor is listed in the official OpenTelemetry processor index
Contrib tail_sampling has a rate_limiting policy (token bucket, spans_per_second), a partial analogue the agent could read in the snapshot
Repository licence is Apache-2.0 (taken from GitHub API source_facts; not re-fetched)

spike_plan.kill_if: The pruned build needs over 16 GB or cannot be made offline, or the fake clock is reachable only through internal state so public-API tests cannot control time
spike_plan.pass_if: Pruned snapshot builds offline in under about 1 h, the skeleton registers in the builder, the fake clock is injectable through a public API, and 20 table cases pass deterministically across three runs
steps: In a throwaway container with network, clone contrib at a7e7ca4 and run go mod vendor on a pruned builder config containing only the processors and receivers the reference needs, timing it
Confirm a minimal processor skeleton (factory, config Validate, consumer for traces/logs/metrics) compiles against the pinned contrib module versions and registers in a builder config
Check whether the processor can take an injected clock through a public option or only an internal field; if internal, plan a public hook in the reference
Write about 20 table cases (admit under limit, drop over limit, burst, per-key isolation, invalid config) against a fake clock and run them three times to check determinism
Run the neighbouring processors' existing test suites on the pruned snapshot to measure regression-gate time and flakiness

v1.summary: Seed S-im-093 is a real open issue (#35204, no PR, unmerged) at the pinned v0.163.0 release of an Apache-2.0 repo, and no public implementation exists, so lookup is none. It is viable as an 8 h implementation task, conditional on the bundle shipping a complete public-API config spec, since the config schema is invented by us and hidden tests would otherwise encode it arbitrarily.

v2.note: A single feature of roughly 1500 lines including tests and docs, with 6 frontier hours in an 8h tier, sits at the DeepSWE calibration point. The tail_sampling rate-limiting policy is in the snapshot as a template. The issue is design-only, so the config schema, error semantics and fake-clock hook are our invention. Hidden tests on our own schema are a few hundred hand-written cases, and alternative valid designs would fail them.
